analysis:
The PR changes only documentation (docs/operations/provider-release.md, lines 311-320) and a release-pipeline unit test (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py, hunk at lines 177-185). No runtime provider, coordinator protocol, attestation, key-custody or encryption code changed.

The doc change says `qualify-sdk` pins DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT to `prod`, so SDK tests see production defaults on every branch. On `dev`, an unset value would compile the dev identity. This is a CI qualification-hygiene change and a security-neutral clarification. The test hardening is stricter than before. It asserts the job-level env is exactly `prod`, that the variable is named once, and that the resolved-environment selector is absent from qualify-sdk. This reduces the risk of test lanes silently compiling a dev or staging identity and of dev/prod identity confusion (A-011, T-034 tangentially). It does not weaken any control.

I also read the rest of the doc head text. Its descriptions of signing, staging, publication and Developer ID verification, plus the dev/staging identity separation, match the TB-011 and TB-002 trust model. The sections on durable build qualification registration, no admin approval in the normal path, and runtime Apple verification remaining required also match. The doc states that official registration does not itself grant serving authority, which is consistent with T-052 and T-054.

Open question for later passes: the doc asserts that `provider-swift/Package.swift` behavior and the `.github/workflows/release-provider.yml` qualify-sdk job really set `prod`. Neither file is in this batch, so the claim is unverified here. The dev-branch lane note that review is not enforced on `dev` is a pre-existing documented gap, not introduced here. No finding.
